# Norwegian plain language

Use this skill for Norwegian UI text, documentation, error messages and product text.

## Language form

- Read the surrounding text first.
- Preserve each file's Bokmål or Nynorsk form. Ask if one text mixes forms or new text has no language context.
- Domain terms, names, code and quotes are not mixed language forms.

## Write clearly

- Start with what the reader needs to know or do. Use active verbs, one idea per sentence and one topic per paragraph.
- Use the project's terminology, otherwise [Termportalen](https://www.termportalen.no/) for the relevant domain and language form. Explain precise technical terms instead of replacing them with inaccurate simpler words.
- Remove filler, repetition, buzzwords, superlatives and unnecessary anglicisms.
- Preserve facts and domain decisions. Do not add claims unsupported by the source.
- Write inclusively and directly. Avoid unclear pronouns.

## UI text

- Button: the action or result.
- Link: where it leads. Button and link text must make sense alone; avoid generic "Click here" or "Read more".
- Error message: what happened and what the user can do.
- Help text: guidance for the field or choice, not internal details.
- Confirmation: exactly what was saved, sent or changed.
- Use the same term in labels, validation, navigation and confirmations.
- Do not insert line breaks inside messages in an error summary; allow normal text wrapping.

Ask before changing domain meaning, restructuring a whole page or removing sections. Read the text in its full user flow. Recommend user testing for important or high-risk text; your own review does not prove users understand it. See [Språkrådet](https://sprakradet.no/klarsprak/).
